## Locked numbers — Table 2 logreg

**Cohort:** n=2,147 (complete-case M037 cohort post-mig_286)
**Outcome:** LN_pos (N1 vs N0); n_events = 1,050 (49% LN+ rate)
**Predictor of interest:** family_hx_thyroid (n_present = 133)

### Logreg results (OR + 95% CI)

| Predictor | aOR | 95% CI | p |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Intercept | 1.35 | (1.00–1.82) | 0.049 |
| **Male sex** | **1.81** | (1.49–2.21) | **<0.0001** |
| **Age (per year)** | **0.98** | (0.98–0.99) | **<0.0001** |
| **Tumor size (per cm)** | **1.18** | (1.12–1.24) | **<0.0001** |
| Family hx thyroid | 1.05 | (0.74–1.51) | 0.770 |

**Pseudo-R² (McFadden):** 0.040
**LR vs null χ²:** 119, df=4

---

## Headlines

1. **Family hx of thyroid cancer is NOT an independent predictor of LN metastasis** (aOR 1.05, p=0.77) — counter to the "syndromic" assumption; consistent with most thyroid CA being sporadic
2. **Male sex** is the strongest categorical predictor (aOR 1.81, p<0.0001)
3. **Younger age** + **larger tumor** are the dominant continuous predictors

The null family-hx finding is a publishable result post-mig_281 because the covariate is now adequately measured (was 4% coverage, now ~30% in the M037 cohort).
